title: Black-Box Embedding Inversion Attack on Vector Databases

problem.claim: Outsourced vector databases and image embedding services may expose sensitive visual information.

gap.claim: Existing image embedding inversion attacks typically require access to model architecture or parameters, which is unavailable in outsourced settings.

contributions.claim: A black-box image embedding inversion attack reconstructs images using only query access to an embedding model or API.
An in-distribution auxiliary dataset is used to train a conditional diffusion model aligned with the private image domain.
The approach uses embedding-guided cross-attention and latent-space diffusion with deterministic decoding through a pretrained VQGAN.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their black-box image embedding inversion attack as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three real-world datasets and three embedding models reportedly show significant outperformance over four state-of-the-art baselines.
The latent-space diffusion design reportedly reduces computational cost while preserving structural and perceptual fidelity.

narrative_sequence.summary: Vector databases are central to modern data science applications.
Embeddings are outsourced for scalability despite privacy risks from information leakage.
Existing image embedding attacks generally assume access unavailable in outsourced settings.
The paper proposes a black-box inversion attack based on conditional diffusion, cross-attention, and latent-space generation.
The authors report benchmark improvements and conclude that image embeddings can expose sensitive visual information.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative reconstruction metrics or experimental results.
The abstract does not specify the datasets, embedding models, baselines, or query budgets.
The abstract does not describe privacy defenses or mitigation effectiveness.
